findings.reason: The 'Resolve source workflow run ID' step declares `env:` at line 29 and again at line 32. GitHub Actions rejects duplicate mapping keys when it parses a workflow, so the whole file fails validation and no workflow_run or workflow_dispatch run starts.
findings.claim: The duplicate env key makes the remediation workflow invalid, so neither automatic nor manual runs work.
findings.evidence: The resolver step defines env twice at lines 29 and 32; strict YAML validation rejects line 32 as a duplicate mapping key.

members.claim: The duplicate env key makes the remediation workflow invalid, preventing automatic and manual runs.
members.evidence: The resolver step defines env twice at lines 29 and 32; strict YAML validation rejects line 32 as a duplicate mapping key.

findings.reason: The if/elif chain has two `else` branches (lines 41 and 94). Once the YAML block indentation is stripped, the `PY` terminators still have two leading spaces, and a plain `<<'PY'` heredoc does not accept that, so it never closes. Bash fails to parse the script, and this step runs on every trigger path, so the workflow cannot work even after the env duplicate is fixed.
findings.claim: The run-ID resolver has invalid shell syntax, so it never reaches artifact processing.
findings.evidence: The conditional has two else branches, at lines 41 and 94, and its PY heredoc terminators retain leading spaces after YAML indentation is removed; bash -n on the extracted step exits 2 with an unexpected-end-of-file error.

members.claim: The run-ID resolver contains invalid shell syntax, preventing it from reaching artifact processing.
members.evidence: The conditional has two else branches, at lines 41 and 94, and its PY heredoc terminators retain leading spaces after YAML indentation is removed; bash -n on the extracted step exits 2 with an unexpected-end-of-file error.

findings.reason: Line 13 runs the job only when `github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'`. A maintainer's push to the PR branch fires pull_request synchronize with the maintainer as actor, so the job is skipped and the new head is never scanned. Lowered from high to medium: it needs a human push to a bot PR rather than happening on the normal Dependabot path.
findings.claim: Gating on github.actor skips the vulnerability scan when a maintainer pushes to a Dependabot PR.
findings.evidence: A maintainer push triggers pull_request synchronization with the maintainer as github.actor; the condition github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' then skips the entire job, although the PR remains Dependabot-authored.

members.claim: Checking the event actor skips vulnerability scanning when a maintainer pushes changes to a Dependabot PR.
members.evidence: A maintainer push triggers pull_request synchronization with the maintainer as github.actor; the condition github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' then skips the entire job, although the PR remains Dependabot-authored.

findings.reason: Lines 37-38 put `${{ inputs.run_id }}` straight into the bash script rather than passing it through env, so `$(...)` in the value would run with GH_TOKEN available. Lowered to low: only users with write access can trigger workflow_dispatch, and they can already change workflows, so this is a hardening defect rather than a privilege escalation.
findings.claim: run_id is interpolated directly into shell source, which allows command injection.
findings.evidence: The unrestricted string input is embedded directly inside double-quoted shell expressions at lines 37–38; a value containing $(command) becomes executable command substitution in a step holding GH_TOKEN, whose workflow permissions include issues: write.

members.claim: Direct interpolation of run_id into shell source permits command injection once the resolver's syntax errors are repaired.
members.evidence: The unrestricted string input is embedded directly inside double-quoted shell expressions at lines 37–38; a value containing $(command) becomes executable command substitution in a step holding GH_TOKEN, whose workflow permissions include issues: write.

findings.reason: Line 292 sets has_recommendations to "false" when nothing is fixable, and the only issue step (line 319) runs only when it is 'true'. No step updates or closes an existing issue, so once everything is fixed the open issue still lists the old recommendations.
findings.claim: When no fixable vulnerabilities remain, the existing remediation issue keeps showing outdated recommendations.
findings.evidence: The report sets has_recommendations to false when recommendations are empty, while the only issue-update step requires true; there is no path to clear or close an existing issue after remediation.

members.claim: A scan with no remaining fixable vulnerabilities leaves the previous remediation issue displaying obsolete recommendations.
members.evidence: The report sets has_recommendations to false when recommendations are empty, while the only issue-update step requires true; there is no path to clear or close an existing issue after remediation.
